# Fast Confirmation Rule (FCR) for Ethereum

> Fast confirmation is complementary to finality, with additional network and stake assumptions.

## Timing

The homepage uses 24 seconds as an illustrative headline. The production guide describes about 12–24 seconds in favorable conditions. Confirmation can take longer or stall. Compared with a 13-minute (780-second) finality baseline, 24 seconds is 32.5× faster and about 97% less waiting. This is not a guaranteed upper bound or faster finality. Post-Glamsterdam timing needs technical confirmation; no future fork is implied to be live.

## Production guide

https://fastconfirm.it/docs/production

Draft based on PR #23 dated September 30, 2026; reconciliation with the current source is outstanding. The adversarial-stake section has an unresolved validator-sampling passage requiring Derek/Francesco review. Consult the formal paper for precise safety assumptions: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.00549v4

## Adoption

Verify client and RPC support and safe-tag semantics before use. Use multiple independent implementations/providers agreeing on the same block hash, monitor freshness, and define disagreement and finality fallback policies. Consider finality for large transfers and optional k-deep checks. Fast confirmation can stall, and safety assumption violations or bugs can cause reorgs; fallback does not undo an earlier false confirmation.

## Use cases

Exchanges, supported cross-chain bridges, L2s, RPC/infrastructure providers, asset issuers and solvers. Support depends on client, asset and route. Chainlink's September 28 CCIP 2.0 announcement describes FCR support when it launches, not verified user activation: https://chain.link/blog/introducing-ccip-2-0
